q: 把 LLD 设计流程五个阶段按依赖顺序排好：
q_en: Put the five LLD design phases in dependency order.
steps: 实现核心方法并验证场景
why: 先澄清范围，再把需求落到实体、类状态和核心方法；最后用走查和 follow-up 检查设计是否站得住。
why_en: Clarify scope first, then derive entities, classes, and core methods before validating the design with a walkthrough.
tradeoff: 先建立结构与契约 vs 直接写代码或先聊扩展
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确跳到某个 follow-up，就先回答它，再把主线拉回剩余阶段。

termDefinitions.meaning: 低层设计面试，重点是把小范围需求拆成类、状态、方法和核心逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Low-Level Design focuses on turning a small scoped problem into classes, state, methods, and core logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试官在主设计后追加的变化或扩展问题，用来检查设计能否演进。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A follow-up is an added change or extension question used to test whether the design can evolve.

diagram:
flowchart TD
A["clarify requirements"] --> B["extract entities"]
B --> C["design class state and behavior"]
C --> D["implement core method"]
D --> E["walk through scenario"]
E --> F["discuss follow-ups"]

scenario: 你正在把「设计 Tic Tac Toe」这句话需求变成可设计的 spec，逐条追问细节。
scenario_en: You are turning the prompt "Design Tic Tac Toe" into a designable spec by asking clarifying questions.
q: 下面哪些追问的答案会直接改变实体或类的设计？（多选）
q_en: Which clarifying answers would directly change the entity or class design? (Select all that apply.)
options: 落子按钮用什么颜色（不影响任何实体或方法签名）
是否要支持 AI 对手（决定要不要为落子逻辑引入 Strategy 接口）
怎样判定获胜或平局（决定 Board 要实现哪些检查方法）
非法操作返回 false 还是抛异常（决定方法的错误处理契约）
options_en: What color the move button is (does not affect any entity or method signature).
Whether an AI opponent is needed (decides if move selection needs a Strategy interface).
How a win or draw is determined (decides which check methods Board must implement).
Whether invalid moves return false or throw (decides the method's error-handling contract).
why: 会改变状态、规则或错误契约的问题才会改类模型；按钮颜色这类展示细节不该挤进核心设计。
why_en: Questions about state, rules, or error contracts change the model; button colors usually do not.

rows: 方法返回值或异常设计

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能能力；在这题里指系统是否要自己选择下一步落子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Artificial Intelligence means the system can choose moves on its own in this problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把可替换的算法或策略封装成独立接口，运行时可以互换实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Strategy pattern encapsulates interchangeable algorithms behind a common interface so implementations can be swapped at runtime.

optionExplanations: 按钮颜色只影响样式渲染，不涉及任何字段、状态或方法签名，所以不该问它来定型。
有没有 AI 对手决定落子选择要不要抽象成可替换的 Strategy 接口，直接改变类结构。
胜负判定规则决定 Board 要实现哪些检查方法，是这道题里改动最大的一条追问。
非法操作是返回 false 还是抛异常，会直接写进方法的错误处理契约，所以要先问清楚。
optionExplanations_en: Button color only affects rendering, not any field or method signature, so it shouldn't drive the design.
Whether there's an AI opponent decides if move selection needs a swappable Strategy interface.
Win/draw rules decide which check methods Board must implement, the biggest design lever here.
Whether invalid moves return false or throw becomes part of the method's error-handling contract.

scenario: 题目只给一句话「设计 Tic Tac Toe」，你要把它变成可设计的 spec。
scenario_en: The prompt only says "Design Tic Tac Toe," and you need to turn it into a designable spec.
q: 先追问哪组问题最能定义系统的规则和边界？
q_en: Which set of questions best defines the system rules and scope first?
options: 数据库要分几个分片、CDN 要几个节点
轮流、胜负判定、非法操作、UI/AI 范围
落子逻辑该用哪种设计模式实现
棋盘格子用什么颜色的边框
options_en: How many database shards or CDN nodes to use.
Turn order, win/draw rules, invalid-move handling, and whether UI or AI is in scope.
Which design pattern to use for move logic.
What border color the board cells should have.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目明确是在线多人游戏平台，才需要讨论网络、分片和部署。
tradeoff: 规则与范围澄清 vs 过早跳到实现细节或视觉样式
why: 第一轮要先锁定轮流规则、结束条件和非法输入；模式、分片和视觉样式都依赖这些边界。
why_en: Lock down turns, end states, and invalid moves first; patterns, sharding, and visuals come after scope is clear.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把静态内容缓存到离用户更近的节点，和游戏规则无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches static content on servers closer to users and has nothing to do with game rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户界面层，负责展示和输入，不应该先决定核心游戏规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A User Interface handles display and input, and it should not define the core game rules first.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能能力；如果纳入范围，会影响落子策略和类边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Artificial Intelligence would affect move-selection strategy and class boundaries if it is in scope.

optionExplanations: 分片和 CDN 节点数属于扩展性问题，游戏规则还没定就先问部署规模，是本末倒置。
轮流、胜负、非法操作和 UI/AI 范围一次性锁定了规则边界，后续设计都建立在它上面。
该用哪种设计模式是实现细节，规则都还没定，先讨论模式只会分散注意力。
格子边框颜色是纯视觉样式，不会影响任何一个方法或状态字段。
optionExplanations_en: Shard count and CDN nodes are scaling concerns; asking about deployment before rules are set is backwards.
Turn order, win/draw, invalid moves, and UI/AI scope lock down the rule boundary everything else depends on.
Which design pattern to use is an implementation detail, pointless before the rules even exist.
Cell border color is pure visual styling and touches no method or state field.

q: 补全需求阶段产出：
q_en: Complete the requirement-phase output:
text: 需求阶段要写下核心 Requirements，也要写下明确的 {{Out of Scope}}——被排除的功能不需要设计对应的实体或接口，这样类模型才不会{{膨胀}}。
why: Out of Scope 是防膨胀用的边界：排除网络对战，就不要为它建 NetworkManager 或协议接口。
why_en: Out-of-scope boundaries keep the model lean; if networking is excluded, skip NetworkManager and protocol APIs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 明确不在本轮设计范围内的功能，面试中先记下但不为它建核心实体或接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Out of scope means a feature is explicitly excluded from this design round, so you note it but do not model core entities or APIs for it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责网络连接或消息收发的组件；网络对战不在范围内时不需要设计它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A NetworkManager handles network connections or messages; it is unnecessary when networked play is out of scope.

scenario: 你正在把一份需求文档拆解成候选类，需要决定哪些名词值得单独建模成实体。
scenario_en: You are splitting a requirements document into candidate classes and deciding which nouns deserve their own entity.
q: 判断一个名词是否该单独建成实体时，哪些提问有帮助？（多选）
q_en: Which questions help decide whether a noun should become its own entity? (Select all that apply.)
options: 它是否维护会变化的状态
它被其他类引用的次数是否够多
它是否执行或约束重要规则
它是否只是别的对象上的一个字段
options_en: Does it hold state that changes over time?
Is it referenced by enough other classes?
Does it enforce or constrain an important rule?
Is it really just a field on another object?
why: 我会看它是否拥有会变状态或规则；如果只是别的对象上的值，就留成字段，别因为被引用多就硬拆类。
why_en: Model it as an entity when it owns changing state or rules; leave simple attached data as a field.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在设计里有独立身份、状态或规则归属的业务对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An entity is a domain object with its own identity, state, or rule ownership.

optionExplanations: 会随时间变化的状态是最强的实体信号，说明它需要自己的生命周期管理。
被引用次数多不代表该拆成类，一个常量或简单值也可能被到处引用。
如果它执行或约束一条重要规则，把规则和状态绑在一起才是它该独立成实体的理由。
如果它只是挂在别的对象上的一个值，硬拆成实体反而制造多余的类。
optionExplanations_en: State that changes over time is the strongest entity signal; it needs its own lifecycle.
Being referenced a lot doesn't make something an entity; a plain constant can be widely referenced too.
If it enforces or constrains an important rule, bundling that rule with its state is reason enough to model it separately.
If it's really just a value attached to another object, splitting it out only creates an extra class.

scenario: Tic Tac Toe 的需求已经确认：两个玩家、3x3 棋盘、落子、胜负和平局。
scenario_en: The Tic Tac Toe requirements are confirmed: two players, a 3x3 board, moves, wins, and draws.
q: 最合理的初始实体集合是？
q_en: What is the most reasonable initial set of entities?
options: DatabaseShard、Cache、CDN
MouseEvent、Pixel、Theme
Game、Board、Player
Factory、Builder、Singleton
options_en: DatabaseShard, Cache, and CDN.
MouseEvent, Pixel, and Theme.
Game, Board, and Player.
Factory, Builder, and Singleton.
tradeoff: 职责清晰的领域实体 vs 把基础设施组件或设计模式名当成实体
whenOtherWins: 如果后续加入 AI、网络或可变棋盘尺寸，才考虑额外实体。
why: Game 管流程，Board 管棋盘和胜负检查，Player 表示参与者；这三类正好覆盖需求里的状态所有权。
why_en: Game owns the flow, Board owns the grid and win checks, and Player represents each participant.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库分片，把数据按规则拆到多台数据库上，是基础设施扩展手段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A database shard is one partition of data placed on a separate database for scaling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存保存常用数据副本以减少读取延迟，不是 Tic Tac Toe 的领域实体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache stores frequently used data copies to reduce read latency; it is not a Tic Tac Toe domain entity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，是基础设施组件，不是游戏领域的业务实体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is infrastructure for caching content, not a business entity in the game domain.

termDefinitions.meaning: 鼠标输入事件，属于 UI 交互细节，不是核心游戏领域对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A MouseEvent is a UI input event, not a core game-domain object.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用于封装对象创建逻辑的设计模式，不是一个业务实体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Factory pattern encapsulates object-creation logic; it is not a business entity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过分步骤设置参数来构造复杂对象的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Builder pattern constructs a complex object through a step-by-step configuration process.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证一个类全局只有一个实例的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance globally.

optionExplanations: DatabaseShard、Cache、CDN 是基础设施扩展手段，跟这道题的游戏规则完全无关。
MouseEvent、Pixel、Theme 都是 UI 交互细节，不是承载游戏状态的领域对象。
Game 驱动流程、Board 管棋盘和判胜、Player 代表参与者，三者正好覆盖需求里的状态归属。
Factory、Builder、Singleton 是创建对象的手段，本身不是业务领域里的实体。
optionExplanations_en: DatabaseShard, Cache, and CDN are infrastructure scaling tools unrelated to this game's rules.
MouseEvent, Pixel, and Theme are UI interaction details, not domain objects that own game state.
Game drives the flow, Board owns the grid and win checks, and Player represents each participant, together covering state ownership.
Factory, Builder, and Singleton are ways to construct objects, not business entities themselves.

scenario: 35 分钟的 Tic Tac Toe LLD 面试，已列出 Game、Board、Player，要先画清关系再写代码。
scenario_en: In a 35-minute Tic Tac Toe design interview you already have Game, Board, and Player, and the relationships must be settled before any code.
q: 定义实体关系时，最重要的问题之一是什么？
q_en: What is one of the most important questions when defining entity relationships?
options: 谁在继承体系里继承的类数量最多，越多说明职责越重
谁对外暴露的 public 方法数量最多，方法越多说明越核心
谁在运行时被实例化的次数最频繁，出现越多说明越重要
谁是 orchestrator，谁拥有持久状态，谁依赖谁
options_en: Whether a class inherits from the most classes — more inheritance is assumed to mean more responsibility.
Whether a class exposes the most public methods — more methods is assumed to mean it's more central.
Whether a class gets instantiated most often at runtime — appearing more is assumed to mean it matters more.
Who is the orchestrator, who owns durable state, and who depends on whom.
why: 关系图要回答谁驱动流程、谁拥有状态、谁依赖谁；这些边界决定后面每个类该暴露什么。
why_en: Relationships show who drives the flow, who owns state, and what each class must expose.

termDefinitions.meaning: 驱动主流程、调用其他对象完成整体行为的类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An orchestrator is the class that drives the main workflow by coordinating other objects.

termDefinitions.meaning: 类对外可调用的方法，数量多少不等于职责是否清晰。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A public method is callable from outside the class; method count alone does not prove clear responsibility.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象需要长期保存并影响后续行为的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Durable state is data an object keeps over time and uses to drive later behavior.

optionExplanations: 继承的类数量多少只是结构指标，不代表职责更重，也不会告诉你谁该拥有状态或驱动流程。
public 方法数量多不代表这个类更核心，可能只是接口设计得臃肿。
实例化次数多通常只说明这个类轻量常被复用，不代表它更重要或该拥有状态。
这条问题直接点名了主控流程的类、保存长期状态的类，以及各类之间的依赖方向。
optionExplanations_en: How many classes it inherits from is just a structural stat; more doesn't mean more responsibility, and it doesn't tell you who should own state or drive the flow.
A high public-method count doesn't mean the class is more central; it might just mean a bloated interface.
Getting instantiated often usually just means the class is lightweight and reused a lot, not that it matters more or should own state.
This question names the class that drives the flow, the one holding long-lived state, and how the classes depend on each other.

scenario: 你已经有 Game、Board、Player 三个实体，要开始展开类。
scenario_en: You already have Game, Board, and Player as entities, and now you need to expand them into classes.
q: 通常应先从哪个类开始？
q_en: Which class should you usually start with?
options: 依赖最少的辅助类，比如 Player
orchestrator，例如 Game
最复杂的支持类，比如 Board 的判胜逻辑
所有工具类和辅助方法
options_en: The supporting class with the fewest dependencies, such as Player.
The orchestrator, such as Game.
The most complex supporting class, such as Board's win-checking logic.
All utility classes and helper methods.
tradeoff: 先定驱动主流程的类 vs 先钻进某个支持类的实现细节
whenOtherWins: 如果某个支持类的规则极其复杂，也可以先展开它以尽早暴露风险。
why: 先从 Game 这种 orchestrator 开始，因为它串起主流程；定下它的调用点，Board 和 Player 才知道要暴露什么。
why_en: Start with Game because it coordinates the flow and reveals what Board and Player need to expose.

termDefinitions.meaning: 驱动主流程、调用其他对象完成整体行为的类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An orchestrator is the class that drives the main workflow by coordinating other objects.

termDefinitions.meaning: 棋盘对象，通常负责保存格子状态并提供落子和判胜相关能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Board is the grid object that usually stores cells and supports move and win checks.

optionExplanations: 先画 Player 这种依赖最少的辅助类，反而定不出它要配合谁、该暴露什么方法。
Game 是整条主流程的入口，先框出它要调用谁、传什么参数，两个支持类才知道自己该开放什么接口。
一上来就钻进 Board 判胜逻辑的细节，容易在主流程还没定的情况下白改设计。
把所有工具类和辅助方法都列一遍，抓不到谁在驱动整个游戏往前走。
optionExplanations_en: Starting with a low-dependency helper like Player leaves you unable to tell what it needs to expose or to whom.
Game is the entry point for the whole flow — pin down who it calls and what it passes first, and the two supporting classes know what to expose.
Diving straight into Board's win-check details risks reworking it once the main flow is finally set.
Listing every utility and helper class first doesn't reveal which class actually drives the game forward.

scenario: Tic Tac Toe 面试进入类设计阶段，只剩十分钟定完每个类的字段与方法，之后直接写实现。
scenario_en: You reach the class-design step of a Tic Tac Toe interview with ten minutes left to fix each class fields and methods before coding.
q: 为每个类设计时，应回答哪两个问题？（多选）
q_en: Which two questions should you answer when designing each class? (Select all that apply.)
options: 它是否该直接读写别的类的私有字段
它需要记住什么状态
它能否负责所有事情
它需要提供什么行为或查询
options_en: Should it directly read and write another class's private fields?
What state does it need to remember?
Can it be made responsible for everything?
What behavior or queries does it need to expose?
why: 每个类只先回答两件事：记住什么状态、暴露什么行为；跨类改私有字段或做万能类都会打破职责边界。
why_en: For each class, define its state and behavior; private-field access and god objects break ownership boundaries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读取对象内部状态的方法；它不应该替代真正的业务行为。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A getter reads an object's internal state, but it should not replace real domain behavior.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只应由本类内部访问和维护的字段，用来保护封装边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A private field should be accessed and maintained only inside its own class to preserve encapsulation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 承担过多职责的类，通常会让规则、状态和修改点集中失控。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A god object takes on too many responsibilities, making rules, state, and changes hard to control.

optionExplanations: 跨类直接读写别人的私有字段会绕开封装，让状态变更散落在调用方手里。
先问它要记住什么状态，是划出这个类边界的第一步。
让一个类能负责所有事情，就是典型的万能类，会让规则和状态全挤在一起。
再问它要对外提供什么行为或查询，状态和行为合起来才是完整的类设计。
optionExplanations_en: Reaching into another class's private fields bypasses encapsulation and scatters state changes into callers.
Asking what state it must remember is the first step in drawing that class's boundary.
Letting one class be responsible for everything is exactly how you end up with a god object.
Asking what behavior or queries it should expose completes the class design alongside its state.

scenario: 需求说“两名玩家轮流落子，游戏胜利或平局后结束”。
scenario_en: The requirements say two players take turns, and the game ends on a win or draw.
q: Game 类至少需要哪些状态？
q_en: What state does the Game class need at minimum?
options: board、两个 player、gameState，但省略 currentPlayer 和 winner
只有 board 和 winner，其余用临时变量代替
board、两个 player、currentPlayer、gameState、winner
board、currentPlayer、gameState、winner，但省略两个 player 的引用
options_en: board, both players, and gameState — but missing currentPlayer and winner.
Only board and winner, with everything else in temporary variables.
board, both players, currentPlayer, gameState, and winner.
board, currentPlayer, gameState, and winner — but missing references to both players.
whenOtherWins: 如果不需要单独查询 winner，可由 board 状态推导；但显式字段更不容易漏判胜负。
tradeoff: 状态完备覆盖判定条件 vs 用临时变量或省略字段图省事
why: 状态要从规则倒推：currentPlayer 决定轮到谁，两个 player 引用让 Game 能切换回合并记录赢家。
why_en: Derive state from the rules: currentPlayer controls turns, and player references let Game switch turns and record the winner.

termDefinitions.meaning: 当前轮到落子的玩家引用，用来校验出手者并决定下一回合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: currentPlayer points to the player whose turn it is and is used to validate and advance moves.

termDefinitions.meaning: 游戏当前所处的状态，例如进行中、获胜或平局。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gameState tracks whether the game is in progress, won, or drawn.

termDefinitions.meaning: 获胜玩家的引用；没有赢家时通常为空。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: winner points to the winning player, or stays null when nobody has won.

optionExplanations: 缺了 currentPlayer 就没法知道该轮到谁落子，缺了 winner 就没法记录结果。
只留 board 和 winner，靠临时变量凑轮次和进度，逻辑会散落在方法之间。
board、两个 player、currentPlayer、gameState、winner 齐了，正好覆盖轮次、进度和结果三件事。
省掉两个 player 的引用，Game 就没法在切换回合或判定赢家时拿到具体玩家对象。
optionExplanations_en: Without currentPlayer you can't tell whose turn it is, and without winner you can't record the result.
Keeping only board and winner forces turn and progress tracking into scattered temp variables.
board, both players, currentPlayer, gameState, and winner together cover turns, progress, and the result.
Dropping the player references leaves Game with no actual player object to switch turns or record a winner.

scenario: 需求需要玩家落子、查询当前玩家、查看游戏状态和赢家。
scenario_en: The requirements need players to move, query the current player, and inspect the game state and winner.
q: Game API 的合理方法集合是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable method set for the Game API?
options: makeMove 和 getBoard 两个方法，UI 没法查到该谁落子或赢家
makeMove、getCurrentPlayer、getGameState 三个方法，游戏结束却查不到赢家是谁
只保留 makeMove 一个方法，调用方连该谁落子都问不到
makeMove、getCurrentPlayer、getGameState、getWinner、getBoard
options_en: makeMove and getBoard — the UI can't tell whose turn it is or who won.
makeMove, getCurrentPlayer, and getGameState — but once the game ends there's still no way to query the winner.
Only the single method makeMove — callers can't even ask whose turn it is.
makeMove, getCurrentPlayer, getGameState, getWinner, and getBoard.
tradeoff: 覆盖需求隐含的全部操作和查询 vs 只实现动作、遗漏查询方法
whenOtherWins: 如果只要求展示核心行为，可以先只实现 makeMove，getter 留到有时间再补。
why: API 要覆盖需求里的动作和查询；少 getCurrentPlayer 或 getWinner，调用方就查不到轮次或结果。
why_en: The API must cover required actions and queries; without getCurrentPlayer or getWinner, callers cannot read turn or result state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个类对外暴露的方法集合，调用方通过它与该类交互。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is the set of methods a class exposes for other code to interact with it.

optionExplanations: 只有 makeMove 和 getBoard，调用方查不到轮到谁、也查不到赢家。
补了轮次和状态查询，却漏了 getWinner，游戏结束后调用方拿不到结果。
只暴露 makeMove，调用方连当前该谁落子都问不到，几乎没法驱动 UI。
makeMove 加四个查询方法，正好覆盖需求里要问的轮次、状态、赢家和棋盘。
optionExplanations_en: With only makeMove and getBoard, callers can't tell whose turn it is or who won.
Turn and state queries are covered, but missing getWinner leaves callers with no result once the game ends.
Exposing only makeMove means callers can't even ask whose turn it is, which barely drives a UI.
makeMove plus four query methods covers exactly what the requirements need: turn, state, winner, and board.

scenario: Tic Tac Toe 里多处都要校验落子合法性，规则被放进拥有格子矩阵的 Board，而非各自取 grid 判断。
scenario_en: Several call sites in Tic Tac Toe must validate a move, so the rule lives inside Board, which owns the grid, instead of each caller reading the grid.
q: “规则放在拥有相关状态的实体里”体现了什么原则？
q_en: Which principle is shown by putting rules inside the entity that owns the relevant state?
options: 封装（Tell, Don't Ask 原则）
遇事都用全局变量，图省事绕开类边界，谁都能改
干脆把所有业务逻辑都塞进 UI 层里
不断叠加继承层级，靠子类复用代码来解决
options_en: Encapsulation (the Tell, Don't Ask principle).
Reaching for global variables so any code can dodge class boundaries and mutate state.
Dumping all the business logic straight into the UI layer.
Piling on inheritance layers to reuse code through subclassing.
why: 拥有状态的对象也该执行相关规则；不要把内部数据交给外部调用方拼判断，否则 bug 会散在多处。
why_en: The object that owns the state should enforce the rule; leaking data outward scatters bugs across callers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把状态和操作该状态的逻辑绑定在同一个类里，不对外暴露内部细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation bundles state with the logic that operates on it and hides internal details from callers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让对象自己执行操作，而不是先问出它的内部状态再由外部决定怎么做。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tell, Don't Ask means telling an object to perform an action instead of asking for its internal state and deciding externally.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户界面层，负责展示和输入，不应承载核心业务规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A User Interface handles display and input, and should not own core business rules.

optionExplanations: 谁拥有状态谁就执行相关规则，这正是封装和 Tell, Don't Ask 的做法。
全局变量会让任何代码都能改状态，规则反而无处安身。
把逻辑全塞进 UI，会让核心规则跟着界面变化一起被改坏。
过度继承是在拿类层级解决状态归属问题，跟这条原则没关系。
optionExplanations_en: The object that owns the state enforces its own rules, exactly what encapsulation and Tell, Don't Ask mean.
Global variables let any code mutate state, leaving the rule with no real owner.
Cramming all logic into the UI ties core rules to whatever the interface happens to do.
Over-inheritance tries to solve state ownership with a class hierarchy, a different problem entirely.

q: 把实现核心方法的推荐顺序排好：
q_en: Put the recommended core-method implementation sequence in order.
steps: 枚举非法输入、非法状态等边界情况
把正常流程写成清晰伪代码
必要时补充返回值和状态变化
why: 先口头跑主流程，让面试官知道方法正常怎么走；再补非法输入和非法状态，最后写成伪代码和状态变化。
why_en: Walk the happy path first, then add invalid inputs and states before writing pseudocode and state changes.
tradeoff: 先讲主流程再补边界 vs 一开始陷入分支细节
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官要求直接写代码，就边写边口头标出 happy path 和边界检查。
diagram:
flowchart TD
A["walk happy path"] --> B["list invalid states and inputs"]
B --> C["write clear pseudocode"]
C --> D["name return values"]
D --> E["show state changes"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 没有异常或错误发生时的主流程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The happy path is the main flow when nothing goes wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接近代码结构但不绑定具体语言语法的表达方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pseudocode describes code-like logic without committing to a specific programming language syntax.

scenario: 你要实现 Tic Tac Toe 的 makeMove，展示状态检查、落子、胜负和平局处理。
scenario_en: You are implementing Tic Tac Toe's makeMove to show state checks, placing a mark, win handling, and draw handling.
q: 这段伪代码最重要的结构特征是什么？
q_en: What is the most important structural feature of this pseudocode?
codeSample:
makeMove(player, row, col):
    if state != IN_PROGRESS or player != currentPlayer: return false
    if not board.canPlace(row, col): return false
    board.placeMark(row, col, player.mark)
    if board.checkWin(row, col, player.mark):
        state, winner = WON, player
    elif board.isFull():
        state = DRAW
    else:
        currentPlayer = otherPlayer()
    return true
options: 把所有规则放到 UI
先拒绝非法状态和动作，再执行状态转换
忽略 currentPlayer
只实现 reset
options_en: Put all the rules in the UI layer.
Reject illegal state or moves first, then apply the state transition.
Ignore currentPlayer entirely.
Only implement reset.
tradeoff: 前置校验保证不变量 vs 直接改状态、事后再补校验
whenOtherWins: 如果要用异常表达失败而不是布尔返回值，可以把 return false 换成 throw，但校验-变更-判定终局的顺序不变。
why: 这段代码先用 guard clause 拒绝非法状态和动作，再落子、判胜负、切回合；顺序清楚才不容易破坏不变量。
why_en: Use guard clauses first, then place the mark, check terminal states, and switch turns so invariants stay intact.
diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
[*] --> IN_PROGRESS
IN_PROGRESS --> WON : checkWin
IN_PROGRESS --> DRAW : board full
IN_PROGRESS --> IN_PROGRESS : valid non-terminal move
WON --> [*]
DRAW --> [*]

termDefinitions.meaning: 函数开头用来提前拒绝非法输入或非法状态的判断语句。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guard clause is an early check that rejects invalid input or state before the main logic runs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户界面层，只负责展示和输入，不应该保存 Tic Tac Toe 的核心规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A User Interface handles display and input, and should not store Tic Tac Toe's core rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 当前轮到落子的玩家，用来拒绝非本回合玩家的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: currentPlayer is the player whose turn it is and is used to reject out-of-turn moves.

termDefinitions.meaning: Game 的三种状态：进行中、已获胜、已平局。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IN_PROGRESS, WON, and DRAW are the three states a Game can be in.

optionExplanations: 代码里根本没有 UI，规则全在 makeMove 里执行，这个说法对不上代码结构。
方法开头的 guard clause 先把不合法的状态和越权动作挡在外面，然后才推进落子、判定和换手。
代码第一行就用 currentPlayer 校验出手者，说忽略它跟代码直接矛盾。
这段代码根本没有 reset 方法，只实现了落子和终局判断。
optionExplanations_en: There's no UI in this snippet at all; every rule runs inside makeMove, so this doesn't match the structure.
The guard clauses up front block illegal state or out-of-turn moves, then the code moves on to placing the mark, checking the result, and switching turns.
The very first check validates currentPlayer, so claiming it's ignored contradicts the code.
This snippet has no reset method at all; it only implements placing a move and checking terminal states.

scenario: 45 分钟的 LLD 面试只剩 15 分钟实现核心 makeMove，你在犹豫要不要先加一层 Factory。
scenario_en: With 15 minutes left in a 45-minute design interview to implement the core makeMove, you are debating whether to add a Factory layer first.
q: 在实现阶段强行塞 Singleton、Factory、Builder 等模式的常见风险是什么？
q_en: What is the common risk of forcing Singleton, Factory, or Builder into the implementation phase?
options: 一定提升可读性
能替代需求澄清
过度设计，浪费时间并模糊核心逻辑
保证所有 follow-up 自动解决
options_en: It always improves readability.
It can substitute for requirements clarification.
Overengineering — it wastes time and obscures the core logic.
It guarantees every follow-up question is automatically handled.
why: 模式要服务真实变化点；如果只是为了显得高级，反而会拖慢实现并遮住核心状态转换。
why_en: Patterns help only when they solve real variation; forced patterns hide the core state transition.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证一个类全局只有一个实例的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance globally.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装对象创建逻辑，让调用方不用关心具体子类的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Factory pattern encapsulates object-creation logic so callers do not depend on concrete subclasses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过分步骤设置参数构造复杂对象的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Builder pattern constructs a complex object through a step-by-step configuration process.

optionExplanations: 硬套模式不一定更好读，反而经常让核心状态转换被多一层抽象包住。
模式解决的是代码结构问题，不能替代需求还没澄清这件事。
为了显得高级硬塞 Singleton、Factory，会占用时间还把核心状态转换埋进抽象层。
模式跟 follow-up 是否被覆盖没有必然关系，能不能应对全看设计本身。
optionExplanations_en: Forcing a pattern in doesn't automatically read better; it often buries the core state transition under an extra layer.
Patterns solve structural problems; they can't substitute for requirements that were never clarified.
Forcing in Singleton or Factory just to look sophisticated burns time and buries the core state transition.
Whether follow-ups get handled has nothing to do with using a pattern; that depends on the design itself.

scenario: 你刚写完 makeMove 的伪代码，要用一个具体走查来验证逻辑，而不是只读代码。
scenario_en: You just wrote makeMove pseudocode and need a concrete walkthrough to verify the logic, not just read the code.
q: 一次好的走查应该覆盖哪些内容？（多选）
q_en: What should a good walkthrough cover? (Select all that apply.)
options: 初始状态
只口头描述，不用具体输入输出
每一步操作发生了什么
每步后状态如何变化
options_en: The initial state.
Only a verbal description without concrete inputs and outputs.
What happens on each operation.
How state changes after each step.
why: 走查要从具体初始状态开始，逐步核对每次操作后的状态；这样才能发现没切回合、没触发胜负这类逻辑 bug。
why_en: Start from a concrete initial state and check state after each move to catch missed turn switches or win checks.

termDefinitions.meaning: Tic Tac Toe 的核心落子方法，负责校验、更新棋盘并推进游戏状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: makeMove is the core Tic Tac Toe method that validates a move, updates the board, and advances game state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用具体输入一步步模拟方法执行，检查每一步后的状态是否正确。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A walkthrough simulates concrete inputs step by step and checks the state after each operation.

optionExplanations: 从一个具体的初始状态开始，走查才有一个可核对的起点。
只靠口头描述、不带具体输入输出，很容易漏掉边界情况却察觉不到。
逐步说清每一步操作做了什么，才能对上代码实际执行的逻辑。
每步后核对状态变化，才抓得到没切回合、没触发胜负这类隐藏 bug。
optionExplanations_en: Starting from a concrete initial state gives the walkthrough a checkable baseline.
A purely verbal description with no concrete input or output makes edge cases easy to miss unnoticed.
Spelling out what each operation actually does is what lets you match it against the real code.
Checking the state after each step is what catches hidden bugs like a missed turn switch or win check.

scenario: 新增需求：Tic Tac Toe 要支持撤销最近一步棋（undo）。
scenario_en: New requirement: Tic Tac Toe must support undoing the most recent move.
q: 最直接的实现方向是什么？
q_en: What is the most direct implementation direction?
options: 把所有类和方法都推倒重写，连带删掉 Board 里已验证过的落子记录方式
在 UI 按钮的点击处理函数里直接改字段，完全跳过 Game 的方法和校验逻辑
给每一个方法都加事务日志，undo 时回滚整个应用状态而不只是棋盘
状态变化集中在 makeMove，加命令历史栈记录落子前状态，undo 弹栈回滚
options_en: Rewrite every class and method from scratch, including how Board already tracks placed marks.
Mutate fields directly inside the UI button's click handler, completely bypassing Game's methods and validation logic.
Add a transaction log to every method and roll back the entire application state, not just the board.
Since state changes are centralized in makeMove, add a command history stack recording the state before each move, and undo pops it.
tradeoff: 复用集中式状态变更点 vs 为 undo 重建应用级事务机制
whenOtherWins: 如果状态很大或历史很多，需要讨论快照、命令差量和内存成本。
why: undo 能自然接上，是因为状态变化都经过 makeMove；在这个入口记录旧状态，回滚就不用改散落的字段。
why_en: Undo fits cleanly because all mutation goes through makeMove, so one history stack can restore the prior state.
diagram:
flowchart TD
A["makeMove is the only state-changing path"] --> B["record successful move"]
B --> C["push prior state to history"]
C --> D["undo pops history"]
D --> E["restore board, turn, state, winner"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户界面层；直接在按钮处理函数里改状态会绕开 Game 的规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A User Interface handles display and input; mutating state in a button handler bypasses Game's rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录状态变更以便恢复或回滚的日志；本题只需要棋局级历史，不需要应用级事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction log records state changes for recovery or rollback; this problem only needs game-level history.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录每次操作前状态的栈结构，undo 时弹出最近一条记录来回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A command history stack records the state before each action so undo can pop the most recent entry and roll back.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一次操作封装成对象，可以记录、排队或撤销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Command pattern encapsulates an action as an object so it can be logged, queued, or undone.

optionExplanations: 把类推倒重写还顺带删掉 Board 记录落子的方式，等于把已验证的设计全部作废。
在 UI 点击处理函数里直接改字段会绕开 Game 的规则，状态变更就不再只经过一个入口。
给每个方法都加事务日志、回滚整个应用状态，远超 undo 一步棋所需要的范围。
makeMove 是棋局里唯一改状态的地方，把落子前的快照存进一个栈，undo 直接弹栈还原即可，改动量最小。
optionExplanations_en: Rewriting every class and deleting how Board tracks marks throws away a design that already works.
Mutating fields directly in a UI click handler bypasses Game's rules, so state changes no longer flow through one entry point.
Adding a transaction log to every method and rolling back the whole app is far more than undoing one move needs.
Since state only ever changes inside makeMove, saving a snapshot there before each move and popping it on undo keeps the change minimal.

q: 补全类设计口诀：
q_en: Complete the class-design rule of thumb:
text: 逐个实体回答两个问题：这个类要记住什么{{状态}}，以及它要提供什么{{行为}}。
why: 状态和行为都要从需求推出来；这样类既不会只是空壳，也不会变成什么都管的万能对象。
why_en: Derive both state and behavior from requirements so the class is neither empty nor a god object.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象需要记住并影响后续行为的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: State is data an object remembers and uses to drive later behavior.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象对外提供的操作或查询，通常来自需求里的动作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Behavior is an operation or query an object exposes, usually derived from required actions.

scenario: 候选人拿到 Tic Tac Toe 需求后立刻开始写 makeMove 的代码，没有先列实体和类结构。
scenario_en: A candidate gets the Tic Tac Toe requirements and immediately writes makeMove without first listing entities and classes.
q: 这样做最可能造成什么技术后果？
q_en: What technical consequence is this most likely to cause?
options: 职责边界不清晰，规则和状态检查散落在各处、后续要返工
跳过设计直接写代码，写出来的代码量更多、速度也更快
跳过设计阶段直接开写，需求反而会在写的过程中自动变清楚
跳过设计阶段，少了抽象层，系统扩展性反而一定更好
options_en: Responsibility boundaries stay unclear — rules and state checks end up scattered and need rework later.
Skipping design and jumping to code usually means writing more code, faster.
Skipping design and just writing code makes requirements automatically clearer as you go.
Skipping the design phase means fewer abstraction layers, which automatically makes the system more extensible.
why: 没先定实体和职责边界，规则就会被随手写进 makeMove；后面再拆回 Board、Game，就是返工。
why_en: Without entity ownership, rules get dumped into makeMove and later must be moved back into Board or Game.

termDefinitions.meaning: Tic Tac Toe 的核心落子方法；它不应该吞掉所有本该属于其他类的规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: makeMove is the core move method, but it should not absorb rules that belong in other classes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个类负责哪些状态和规则的分界线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A responsibility boundary defines which state and rules each class owns.

optionExplanations: 没先分好实体职责，规则往往顺手就塞进了 makeMove，之后要挪回 Board、Game 全是返工成本。
跳过设计确实能更快落笔、写出更多代码，但代码量和速度不等于代码写对了。
跳过设计阶段不会让需求自动变清楚，反而更容易漏掉边界情况。
少了抽象层不代表扩展性更好，职责边界不清反而更难加新功能。
optionExplanations_en: Skip defining who owns which entity, and rules tend to get stuffed into makeMove, and untangling them into Board and Game afterward is pure rework.
Skipping design does let you write more code faster, but volume and speed aren't the same as writing it correctly.
Skipping the design phase doesn't make requirements clearer on its own; it usually just means more missed edge cases.
Fewer abstraction layers doesn't mean better extensibility; unclear ownership makes adding features harder, not easier.

scenario: 候选人在类设计阶段反复打磨每一个 getter 和辅助方法的细节。
scenario_en: During class design, the candidate keeps polishing every getter and helper method in detail.
q: 这样做最可能导致什么技术后果？
q_en: What technical consequence is this most likely to lead to?
options: 花更多时间打磨细节，需求一定会变得更准确
核心方法的状态转换逻辑没写完，也没时间走查验证
打磨到足够细致后，就不需要再实现任何方法
把每个方法都打磨完善，系统会自动变得可扩展
options_en: Spending more time polishing details always makes requirements more accurate.
The core state-transition logic never gets finished, and there is no time left to verify it.
Once details are polished enough, no methods need to be implemented at all.
Polishing every method automatically makes the system more extensible.
why: getter 和 helper 细节会吃掉时间；真正证明设计的，是核心状态转换能跑通并被走查验证。
why_en: Getter and helper details burn time; the design is proven by core state transitions and a walkthrough.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读取对象状态的方法；通常不如核心状态转换能展示设计能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A getter reads object state and usually shows less design skill than the core transition logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 辅助主流程的小方法，应服务核心逻辑而不是抢走实现时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A helper method supports the main flow and should not consume time needed for core logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象从一个状态变到另一个状态的规则和动作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A state transition is the rule and action that move an object from one state to another.

optionExplanations: 打磨 getter 细节花的是实现时间，不会让需求本身变得更准确。
时间都耗在 getter 和辅助方法上，核心状态转换写不完，也没机会走查验证。
细节打磨得再精致，核心方法该实现的还是要实现，不会因此被免掉。
打磨每个方法跟系统是否可扩展没有必然联系，职责边界不清才是扩展性的关键。
optionExplanations_en: Polishing getter details spends implementation time; it doesn't make the requirements themselves more accurate.
Time sunk into getters and helpers leaves the core state transition unfinished and unverified.
No amount of polish exempts you from implementing the core methods that actually need to exist.
Polishing every method has no real bearing on extensibility; unclear ownership is what actually hurts it.

scenario: 时间只够实现两个方法，但类里列了很多 getter、reset、helper。
scenario_en: There is only enough time to implement two methods, but the class lists many getters, reset methods, and helpers.
q: 应该优先实现哪些？
q_en: Which methods should you implement first?
options: 所有 getter 方法，因为最容易写对不容易出错
方法体最短的那些，先写完能更快看到进度
定义系统行为和状态转换的核心方法
最像设计模式的方法，能展示设计能力
options_en: All the getter methods, since they're the easiest to get right without bugs.
Whichever method bodies are shortest, since finishing them first shows visible progress faster.
The core methods that define system behavior and state transitions.
Whichever methods look most like a design pattern, since that shows off design skill.
tradeoff: 优先展示状态转换逻辑 vs 优先展示访问器或形式上的模式使用
whenOtherWins: 如果某个查询方法本身包含复杂规则，比如带条件的 getWinner，它也值得优先实现。
why: 优先写能展示系统运转的核心方法；普通 getter 只是读字段，除非它本身包含关键规则。
why_en: Implement the methods that show the system running; plain getters matter only when they encode real rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读取对象内部字段的方法；普通 getter 很少展示核心设计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A getter reads an internal field and rarely demonstrates the core design by itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次操作让系统状态发生可追踪变化的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A state transition is a traceable change in system state caused by an operation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 解决常见设计问题的可复用结构，但不应替代核心业务逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A design pattern is a reusable structure for common design problems, but it should not replace core business logic.

optionExplanations: getter 确实不容易写错，但把所有 getter 实现完，展示的只是读字段的能力，系统还没真正跑起来。
先写完短方法确实看起来进度快，但跟这个方法是否承载核心逻辑没有关系。
先写真正定义行为和状态转换的方法，才能让人看到系统实际在运转。
看起来像设计模式确实容易在讲解时显得有设计感，但并不能证明它承载了核心业务逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: Getters are indeed hard to get wrong, but implementing every getter only demonstrates reading fields; the system still isn't actually running.
Finishing short methods first does look like faster progress, but it has nothing to do with whether they carry core logic.
Writing the methods that actually define behavior and state transitions is what shows the system running.
Looking design-pattern-like does make it sound impressive to explain, but it doesn't prove it carries real business logic.

scenario: makeMove 的核心逻辑写完之后，你要主动补充边界情况。
scenario_en: After the core makeMove logic is written, you need to proactively add edge cases.
q: 哪些边界情况值得主动提出？（多选）
q_en: Which edge cases are worth proactively calling out? (Select all that apply.)
options: 完全无关的未来大功能，例如联机对战
非法输入，例如越界的 row/col
当前状态下不允许的操作，例如游戏已经结束时落子
已被占用的格子
options_en: An unrelated future feature, such as networked multiplayer.
Invalid input, such as an out-of-range row or col.
Operations not allowed in the current state, such as moving after the game has ended.
A cell that is already occupied.
why: 边界情况要贴着 makeMove 的前置条件：坐标、游戏状态、格子占用；联机对战这种未来功能先别混进来。
why_en: Edge cases should match makeMove preconditions: coordinates, game state, and occupied cells, not future networking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 棋盘上的行号和列号，用来定位一次落子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: row and col identify the board cell where a move is placed.

termDefinitions.meaning: Tic Tac Toe 的落子方法，边界检查应围绕它的输入和当前状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: makeMove is the move method, so edge checks should focus on its inputs and current state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过网络让不同设备上的玩家对战，属于额外范围而不是本方法边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Networked multiplayer lets players on different devices play together; it is extra scope, not a makeMove edge case.

optionExplanations: 联机对战是完全独立的未来功能，跟 makeMove 现在的输入或状态毫无关系，先别混进来。
越界的 row/col 会让棋盘写到不存在的格子，必须在落子前拦住。
游戏已经结束还允许落子，会让棋局在终局之后继续被篡改。
格子已被占用还允许落子，会让一步棋覆盖掉另一名玩家的落子。
optionExplanations_en: Networked multiplayer is a totally separate future feature with no bearing on makeMove's current input or state.
An out-of-range row or col would write to a cell that doesn't exist, so it must be blocked before placing a mark.
Allowing moves after the game has ended would let the board keep changing past a final result.
Allowing a move on an occupied cell would let one player's mark overwrite another's.

q: 把 Tic Tac Toe 走查的顺序排好：
q_en: Put the Tic Tac Toe walkthrough sequence in order.
steps: 说明初始棋盘为空且 currentPlayer 为 X
执行 O 的一步并切回 X
执行 X 的一步并切到 O
继续到胜利或平局并确认 state/winner 更新
why: 走查要按具体落子推进，每一步都检查 currentPlayer、state 和 winner；这样才能抓到轮次或终局更新漏掉。
why_en: Trace concrete moves and check currentPlayer, state, and winner after each one.
tradeoff: 具体状态走查 vs 只口头说代码应该能跑
whenOtherWins: 如果时间只剩几十秒，至少走一条能触发胜利或平局的短路径。

termDefinitions.meaning: 当前轮到落子的玩家，走查时每一步都要确认它是否切换正确。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: currentPlayer is the player whose turn it is; a walkthrough should confirm it changes correctly.

termDefinitions.meaning: state 表示游戏是否进行中、获胜或平局；winner 记录获胜者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: state tracks whether the game is running, won, or drawn, while winner stores the winning player.

scenario: 你发现自己准备实现 UI 渲染、AI 对手、网络多人和 undo，但这些都没在需求里。
scenario_en: You notice you are about to implement UI rendering, an AI opponent, networked multiplayer, and undo, but none are in the requirements.
q: 应该怎么处理？
q_en: How should you handle that?
options: 把 UI、AI、网络多人和 undo 全部实现，以此展示自己的能力
删掉已经写好的核心游戏逻辑，腾出时间做这些功能
只实现 UI 渲染，把其余三项都无限期搁置
记为 out of scope 或 follow-up，不塞进核心设计
options_en: Implement UI, AI, networking, and undo all at once to show off capability.
Delete the core game logic you already wrote to make time for these features.
Implement only the UI and leave the other three indefinitely.
Record them as out of scope or follow-ups instead of folding them into the core design.
tradeoff: 先交付确认过的核心需求 vs 提前实现未确认的扩展功能
whenOtherWins: 如果其中某项后来被确认为核心需求，就把它纳入范围并重新评估实体模型。
why: 核心需求先做完整，未确认功能先记到 out of scope 或 follow-up；否则主线会被 UI、AI、网络和 undo 拖散。
why_en: Finish the confirmed core first; park UI, AI, networking, and undo as out of scope or follow-ups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户界面层，负责展示和输入；本题未要求时不应抢占核心设计时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A User Interface handles display and input; if it is not required, it should not consume core design time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能能力；在这题里指系统自动选择落子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Artificial Intelligence means the system can choose moves automatically in this problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 撤销最近一步操作的能力，通常作为扩展而不是基础需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Undo is the ability to reverse the most recent action, usually an extension rather than a base requirement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主设计完成后再讨论的扩展或变化问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A follow-up is an extension or change discussed after the main design.

optionExplanations: 把四个未确认的功能都做一遍，只会占用本该花在核心逻辑上的时间。
为了腾时间删掉已经验证过的核心逻辑，等于拿确定的产出换不确定的功能。
只做 UI 意味着核心游戏规则反而没被优先完成，方向本末倒置。
这四项先归到未确认清单里，主设计照常推进，等被确认成核心需求时再回头展开。
optionExplanations_en: Building all four unconfirmed features just eats time that should go to the confirmed core logic.
Deleting already-verified core logic to make room trades a sure deliverable for an unconfirmed one.
Building only the UI means the actual game rules aren't the priority, which is backwards.
Park all four as unconfirmed for now, keep the core design moving, and expand them later only if they get confirmed as real requirements.

scenario: 你要把 Game 类的设计画出来，既要让人看出它的状态，也要看出它对外暴露的操作。
scenario_en: You need to draw the Game class so the interviewer can see both its state and the operations it exposes.
q: 哪种表示法完整传达了类的设计？
q_en: Which notation fully communicates the class design?
options: State 区列字段类型，方法区列 makeMove 等带参数和返回类型
白板上只写方法名，不写参数、返回类型和状态字段，讨论起来更快
白板上只写 Game 一个单词，觉得细节可以等写代码时再补
把类里所有字段都标成 public，省掉写 getter/setter 的工作量
options_en: A State section listing field types, plus methods like makeMove with parameters and return types.
List only method names on the whiteboard — no parameters, return types, or state fields — since it's faster to talk through.
Write just the word Game on the whiteboard, figuring the details can be filled in once you start coding.
Mark every field in the class public, which saves you from writing getters and setters.
tradeoff: 状态与行为都可核对 vs 只有名字、无法核对封装或契约
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官要求真实代码，可以直接把这个轮廓转成语言里的类定义。
why: 类图要能核对字段类型、方法参数和返回值；把字段全设成 public，只是绕过封装让外部随便改状态。
why_en: Show field types and method signatures; making every field public bypasses encapsulation and lets callers mutate state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 方法名加上参数类型和返回类型，定义了调用契约。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A method signature is the method name plus its parameter and return types, defining the calling contract.

termDefinitions.meaning: 公开访问级别；字段全 public 会让外部代码绕过类自己的规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: public is an access level; public fields let outside code bypass the class's own rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把状态和操作状态的逻辑放在同一个类里，并隐藏内部细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation keeps state and the logic that changes it together while hiding internals.

optionExplanations: State 区列出带类型的字段，加上带参数和返回类型的方法签名，才能核对封装和契约是否成立。
只写方法名确实讨论起来更快，但没有参数和返回类型，别人没法核对调用契约是否正确。
细节确实可以留到写代码时再补，但白板上只写一个 Game，看不出它有什么状态、暴露什么方法，没法当场核对设计。
省掉 getter/setter 确实少写代码，但把所有字段都设成 public 等于放弃封装，外部代码可以绕开规则直接改状态。
optionExplanations_en: A typed State section plus method signatures with parameters and return types is what lets you verify encapsulation and contracts.
Listing only method names is indeed faster to talk through, but without parameters or return types nobody can check the calling contract.
Details can be filled in once coding starts, but writing just the word Game on the board shows neither its state nor what it exposes, so there's nothing to verify on the spot.
Skipping getters and setters does save writing code, but making every field public abandons encapsulation, letting outside code mutate state without going through the class's rules.

q: 补全交付框架总结：
q_en: Complete the delivery-framework summary:
text: LLD 设计要按顺序覆盖：{{需求}}、{{实体关系}}、{{类设计}}、{{核心实现}}、{{验证/扩展}}。
why: 这个顺序不是背模板，而是防漏项：先定范围和结构，再证明核心状态转换能跑通。
why_en: The order prevents omissions: define scope and structure first, then prove the core state transition works.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低层设计面试，重点是类、状态、方法和核心逻辑的交付。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Low-Level Design focuses on delivering classes, state, methods, and core logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统从一个状态变到另一个状态的规则和动作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A state transition is the rule and action that moves a system from one state to another.

scenario: Tic Tac Toe 里「这个格子是否已被占用」这条规则，占用状态只存在 Board 的网格数组里；Game 只持有 board 引用和回合信息。
scenario_en: In Tic Tac Toe, the rule "is this cell already occupied" depends on occupancy state that lives only in Board's grid array; Game just holds a board reference and turn info.
q: 这条占用检查应该放进哪个类？
q_en: Which class should own this occupancy check?
options: 放进 Board，因为占用状态存在它的网格里，规则跟着状态走
放进 Game，把所有规则集中到编排者，其他类只当数据容器
放进 Player，由落子的一方负责检查自己选的格子合不合法
放进调用方，Board 暴露 getGrid() 让调用方读出网格自己判断
options_en: Put it on Board, since the occupancy state lives in its grid and rules follow state.
Put it on Game, centralizing every rule in the orchestrator and leaving other classes as data containers.
Put it on Player, so whoever places the mark checks whether the chosen cell is legal.
Put it on the caller, exposing Board.getGrid() so the caller reads the grid and decides.
tradeoff: 规则跟着状态走（封装） vs 规则集中在编排者
whenOtherWins: 跨多个实体状态的流程规则——比如「现在轮到谁」「游戏是否已结束」——确实属于 Game 这个编排者。
why: 占用状态只存在 Board 里，规则放在拥有状态的类才不必把网格结构暴露出去。代价：Board 不再是纯数据容器，要为每条规则加方法。
why_en: The occupancy state lives only in Board, so putting the rule there avoids exposing the grid; the cost is that Board grows behavior instead of staying a plain container.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把状态和操作该状态的规则放在同一个类里，对外只暴露行为。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation keeps state and the rules that govern it inside one class, exposing only behavior.

termDefinitions.meaning: 驱动主流程的类，负责流程和生命周期规则，比如现在能不能执行这个操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The orchestrator is the class that drives the main workflow and owns lifecycle rules such as whether an operation may run now.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让对象自己管状态并暴露行为，而不是暴露 getter 让调用方取数据后自己判断。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tell, Don't Ask means objects should manage their own state and expose behavior instead of exposing getters for callers to decide.

optionExplanations: 网格是 Board 的私有状态，判定和状态同处一类，接口只需要一个 canPlace。
把数据规则也塞进编排者，Game 必须知道网格的内部结构，改存储方式就要改 Game。
Player 手里没有网格，它无从判断某格是否被占，只能反过来去问 Board。
暴露 getGrid() 等于把判断权交给外部，封装被绕开，每个调用方各判一次。
optionExplanations_en: The grid is Board's private state, so rule and state sit together and the API is just canPlace.
Pushing data rules into the orchestrator forces Game to know the grid's internals, so changing storage changes Game.
Player holds no grid, so it cannot judge occupancy and would have to ask Board anyway.
Exposing getGrid() hands judgement to the outside, bypassing encapsulation so every caller judges separately.

scenario: Board 对外只提供 getGrid() 返回原始网格；占用判定和连线判定由 Game、走查代码和后加的 undo 各自读网格实现。
scenario_en: Board only exposes getGrid() returning the raw grid; occupancy checks and win checks are each re-implemented by Game, the walkthrough code, and a later undo feature.
q: 调用方变多以后，这种设计具体怎么坏掉？
q_en: As callers multiply, how exactly does this design break?
options: 占用判定散在每个调用方，改规则时漏改一处，同一格出现两种判断结果
getGrid() 只是读操作不改状态，因此不会引入任何正确性风险
问题只出在性能层面：每次读整个网格多一次拷贝，判定逻辑本身仍正确
规则最终会自动收敛回 Board，因为调用方都会复用同一个判定函数
options_en: The occupancy rule is duplicated across callers, so missing one when it changes makes the same cell judged two ways.
getGrid() is a read that never mutates state, so it introduces no correctness risk at all.
The only issue is performance: reading the whole grid copies extra data, while the logic stays correct.
Rules converge back into Board on their own, because callers all end up reusing one shared check.
tradeoff: 一个 getter 的小接口 vs 规则只有一份的可维护性
whenOtherWins: 如果网格只被渲染层只读消费、没有任何判定逻辑，直接给一个只读视图是够用的。
why: 规则一旦离开状态所有者就会被复制多份，改判定时漏改一处就出现不一致，而且出错时无法定位是哪个类判错。代价：Board 要为每条规则加方法。
why_en: Once a rule leaves the class owning the state it gets copied, so one missed update makes callers disagree and you can't tell which class judged wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让对象自己管状态并暴露行为，而不是暴露 getter 让调用方取数据后自己判断。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tell, Don't Ask means objects should manage their own state and expose behavior instead of exposing getters for callers to decide.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把状态和操作该状态的规则放在同一个类里，对外只暴露行为。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation keeps state and the rules that govern it inside one class, exposing only behavior.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只把内部字段原样返回的方法；返回可变结构时等于放弃封装。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A getter returns an internal field as-is; returning a mutable structure effectively gives up encapsulation.

optionExplanations: 三处各写一份占用判定，规则一改就有版本漂移，Board 自己反而不是唯一事实来源。
读操作确实不改状态，但风险不在写，而在判定逻辑被复制到多个地方。
多一次拷贝只是常数开销；真正的代价是规则分叉，性能视角看不到它。
复用不会自动发生，赶时间的调用方通常就地再写一遍判断。
optionExplanations_en: Three copies of the occupancy rule drift apart on the first change, so Board stops being the source of truth.
Reads indeed don't mutate, but the risk is not writing — it is the judgement logic being copied around.
An extra copy is constant overhead; the real cost is rule divergence, which a performance lens misses.
Reuse does not happen by itself — a caller under time pressure just rewrites the check inline.

scenario: 类设计讲完，实现阶段只剩约 10 分钟。有的公司只要伪代码，有的要指定语言的接近完整代码，有的只要你口头讲逻辑，而面试官还没说要哪种。
scenario_en: Class design is done and about 10 minutes remain for implementation. Some companies want only pseudo-code, some want near-complete code in a given language, some just want you to talk through it — and the interviewer hasn't said which.
q: 动笔写核心方法前第一个动作是什么？
q_en: What is the first move before writing the core methods?
options: 先问面试官要哪种细节层级：伪代码、完整代码还是口述逻辑
直接用最熟悉的语言写完整可运行代码，细节越全越能体现工程能力
统一写伪代码，因为伪代码在任何公司都是被默认接受的形式
先换成面试官团队常用的语言，即使自己平时不写，也更贴近岗位
options_en: Ask the interviewer which level of detail they want: pseudo-code, full code, or a verbal walkthrough.
Just write complete runnable code in your strongest language — more detail shows more engineering skill.
Always write pseudo-code, since it is the universally accepted default at every company.
Switch to the language the interviewer's team uses, even if you don't write it day to day.
tradeoff: 花十几秒确认期望 vs 按自己的习惯直接开写
whenOtherWins: 如果题面或面试官已经明确说了「用 Python 写完整实现」，就不必再问，直接按指定形式开写。
why: 各家在这一步的期望差别很大，10 分钟不够写错形式再返工，问一句就把风险消掉。代价：可能被要求用你不那么熟的形式。
why_en: Expectations vary a lot company to company, and ten minutes leaves no room to write the wrong format twice, so one question removes the risk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用缩进结构表达逻辑、不绑定具体语言的写法，是实现阶段最常见的默认形式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pseudo-code expresses logic with indentation without committing to a language, and is the most common default in the implementation step.

optionExplanations: 一句确认就锁定形式，剩下的时间全部花在最能体现设计的核心方法上。
写完整代码在只要伪代码的场合会吃光时间，核心状态转换反而讲不完。
伪代码是没说明时的默认，但不是所有公司的要求，当成通用答案会踩坑。
临时换不熟的语言通常是净损失，语法卡顿会挤掉讲逻辑的时间。
optionExplanations_en: One question locks the format so the remaining time goes into the methods that actually show the design.
Full code where pseudo-code suffices burns the clock and leaves the core state transition unfinished.
Pseudo-code is the default when nothing is specified, but treating it as universal misses stricter interviewers.
Switching to an unfamiliar language is usually a net loss — syntax friction eats the time meant for logic.

scenario: 走查 Tic Tac Toe：初始 currentPlayer = X，执行 makeMove(X,0,0) 后你发现 currentPlayer 仍是 X，回合没切换——后面每一步的落子合法性判断都会建立在这个错状态上。
scenario_en: Walking through Tic Tac Toe: currentPlayer starts as X, and after makeMove(X,0,0) you notice currentPlayer is still X — the turn never switched, so every later legality check builds on that wrong state.
q: 发现这个状态错误时该怎么做？
q_en: What should you do the moment you spot this state bug?
options: 当场改掉切换回合的分支，然后重跑这段走查确认状态正确
记下来先走完剩余步骤，等面试官问到再回头修，保持叙述连贯
跳过这一步继续走查，因为走查是讲设计而不是调试具体代码
把它记成边界情况写进 out of scope，说明完整实现留到线下补齐
options_en: Fix the turn-switch branch on the spot, then re-run this trace to confirm the state is right.
Note it, finish the remaining steps, and fix it later if the interviewer brings it up, keeping the narration smooth.
Skip that step and keep going, since a walkthrough is about explaining design, not debugging code.
Record it as an edge case marked out of scope and say the full implementation would be finished offline.
tradeoff: 当场修复换正确性和调试信号 vs 保住叙述节奏留时间给扩展题
whenOtherWins: 如果发现的只是命名或语法瑕疵、不影响状态转换，口头带过即可，不必停下重跑走查。
why: 走查的价值就是在面试官之前抓到状态转换错误，当场修好并重跑本身就是正向的调试信号。代价：修 bug 会吃掉留给扩展追问的几分钟。
why_en: The whole point of the walkthrough is catching a broken state transition before the interviewer does, and fixing it live is itself a positive debugging signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 拿一个具体场景逐步推演代码，检查每步之后的状态是否正确。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A walkthrough traces a concrete scenario step by step, checking the state after each operation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 明确划在本次设计之外的功能，记下来防止范围蔓延。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Out of scope marks features deliberately excluded from this design to prevent scope creep.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次操作之后系统状态该怎么变，比如落子后把 currentPlayer 换成对手。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A state transition is how system state must change after an operation, such as flipping currentPlayer to the opponent after a move.

optionExplanations: 回合没切换会污染后续每一步的判断，改完重跑才能证明这条链现在是对的。
留着不修，后面几步都建立在错状态上，走查结论整体作废。
走查恰恰是为了抓这类逻辑错误；跳过它就放弃了这一步唯一的产出。
回合切换是核心需求里的规则，不是边界情况，划到 out of scope 是躲问题。
optionExplanations_en: An unswitched turn poisons every later check, so only fixing and re-running proves the chain is now correct.
Leaving it unfixed means the remaining steps all run on wrong state, invalidating the whole trace.
Catching exactly this kind of logic error is why you walk through; skipping it forfeits the step's only output.
Turn switching is a core requirement, not an edge case, so marking it out of scope dodges the problem.

scenario: 类设计阶段面试官说「把它画成 UML 图」。你只剩 12 分钟，既要覆盖剩下的类，还要实现核心方法。
scenario_en: During class design the interviewer says "draw that as a UML diagram." You have 12 minutes left to cover the remaining classes and still implement the core methods.
q: 怎么回应最能兼顾进度和配合？
q_en: What response best balances pace with cooperation?
options: 问一句能否用简化类记法代替，通常可以，写得更快也更好讨论
解释 UML 已经过时并拒绝，坚持用自己的记法把设计讲完
按标准 UML 补齐组合、可见性和基数符号，形式正确优先于进度
先画完整 UML，再补一份简化类记法，两种都留在白板上
options_en: Ask whether simplified class notation is acceptable — it usually is, and it's faster to write and discuss.
Explain that UML is outdated, decline, and keep going with your own notation.
Draw proper UML with composition, visibility, and cardinality symbols, putting correctness of form first.
Draw full UML first, then add simplified class notation, leaving both on the whiteboard.
tradeoff: 配合面试官指定的形式 vs 用更快的记法保住实现时间
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确说必须是标准 UML，就照做——不要为记法之争消耗回合。
why: 简化类记法同样能表达字段类型、方法签名和依赖，问一句换掉正式符号通常会被接受，省下的时间留给核心实现。代价：对方坚持时你仍要照画。
why_en: Simplified class notation conveys the same fields, signatures, and dependencies, so asking to swap it in is usually accepted and buys back time for the implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一建模语言，一套带组合、可见性、基数符号的正式建模记法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Unified Modeling Language is a formal notation with symbols for composition, visibility, and cardinality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 白板上用 State 区列字段、方法区列签名的轻量写法，不带 UML 符号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Simplified class notation lists fields under State and method signatures under Behavior, without UML symbols.

termDefinitions.meaning: UML 里标注一个实体关联多少个另一实体的数量关系，如 1 对 2。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality in UML annotates how many instances of one entity relate to another, such as one to two.

optionExplanations: 简化记法照样列出 State 字段和方法签名，信息不少但落笔快得多。
硬顶面试官会把对话变成记法之争，比多画几个符号更贵。
补全组合、可见性和基数符号要花好几分钟，核心方法就没时间写了。
画两遍是纯重复劳动，12 分钟里最不该做的就是同一份设计写两份。
optionExplanations_en: Simplified notation still lists State fields and method signatures — same information, much faster to write.
Pushing back turns the conversation into an argument about notation, costlier than a few extra symbols.
Filling in composition, visibility, and cardinality takes minutes you then can't spend on core methods.
Drawing it twice is pure duplication — the last thing to do with 12 minutes left.
